title: Mall World origin stories
content: I gave up on dream interpretation books when I learned that one man’s Freudian fixation is another man’s cigar, and meanings are as unique as the individual. I’m stuck at home with nasty weather and my mind is fluid right now, so I ask your indulgence! When I was a kid a mall was practically a quest because we were so remote. In grade school Lip Smackers were status symbols because at the time they were huge and you wore them around your neck, and you could only get them at one mall in the area. A Lip Smacker meant you could get out of town on occasion, that’s how deep in the sticks we were. Our principal recreation besides municipal sports programs was church. And in Sunday School we learned that our bodies were just temporarily houses for our souls. I won’t go into details of my horrible childhood except to say I had a nervous breakdown at age 13 started by a dream of utmost devastation where I saw every building around me annihilated. In the years following I came to understand a building in my dreams as an indicator of my state of mind. The mall after all these years is still a quest; I’m trying to find the mall, a specific store or restaurant, or it’s a maze I need to solve to find what I need. Cityscapes can be grand like a Dubai of the mind, or decrepit. If I make it into the mall I often need to find that one perfect thing; if I end up in the district with aristocratic churches or the Avenue of the Shrines, I need a spiritual experience. Always seeking something ultimately within.
